WhatCable sits in your menu bar and reads the cable data your Mac already has access to. Plug in a cable and it tells you in plain English what it can actually do: charging wattage, data speed, display support, Thunderbolt, etc.

Built in Swift/SwiftUI. Open source, free, no tracking.

problems.title: I used the app for a week and to be honest it's far from suitable. Task capture is fast and natural
problems.content: I used the app for a week and to be honest it's far from suitable. Task capture is fast and natural language works great. Kanban is not correct as tasks don't move to the done column on completion. The sync is completely broken on android which I discovered after a few days of work, as the web app was showing a completely different state. Manually syncing did nothing. This is a simple and fundamental feature that should not break so easily. I am now using obsidian with the TaskNotes plugin.

problems.title: Claude Code dies with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in cloud environment
problems.content:
Claude Code dies with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in cloud environment If you put ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the cloud environment, this will cause CC to fail to do anything.

So you were using it because your tests are going to look for it, think again, find another way.

Also, I suspect that is why I had a lot of "Extra usage".

For the whole long history:

https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/54497

Hope this saves some others a lot of headaches!

problems.title: [Feature Request]: task reminder functionality for pages and databases
problems.content:
[Feature Request]: task reminder functionality for pages and databases

### Description

A built-in reminder feature that works in both pages and databases. This feature would allow users:

- Insert a date and time in a page or database record and mark it as a reminder.
- Tag another user when creating a reminder (for example, “`@Dahyun` `@remind next Tuesday 9 AM to review report`”).
- See reminders turn red when they are due today or past due.
- Receive a visual indicator (a badge or icon) next to an “Inbox” or “Notifications” section.
- Get push notifications in the desktop and mobile apps
